headline: Learned models infer tumor-cell and spatial expression from histology, MRI, bulk assays
label: Learned Multimodal Prediction In Cancer
summary: Learned models now predict tumor-cell-specific and spatially resolved quantities from histology, MRI and bulk omics, with external validation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned models that map one measurement modality onto another or fuse several into a shared predictive space, then test them against defined endpoints. Path2Space predicts spatial gene expression from breast cancer histopathology and outperforms 21 methods, and BRIDGE pretrains a histology-to-spatial transcriptomics foundation model on over 600k pairs for few-shot pan-cancer virtual profiling. PRECISE-GBM infers glioblastoma macrophage signatures from MRI across three held-out public cohorts, and TmSNet predicts tumor cell-specific total mRNA expression from mRNA, methylation, miRNA and immune features. A machine-learning framework defines nine conserved spatial ecotypes from over 10 million spatial transcriptomes. What is new is prediction of tumor-cell-specific and spatially resolved quantities from histology, MRI and bulk assays. The R packages and the NSCLC fusion study extend the thread only loosely.
